batches.title: Educational establishment point-context qualification
batches.coverage: Point/context layer only. It does not define a development constraint or catchment boundary; proximity requires a real distance computation, not exact-coordinate equality.

batches.title: Nutrient neutrality catchment exact-boundary qualification
batches.coverage: Natural England-designated catchment geometry is spatially relevant, but a catchment hit alone does not establish scheme-specific nutrient budget, mitigation, or permission outcome.

batches.title: Public transport access node point/proximity qualification
batches.coverage: NaPTAN points are authoritative transport access locations. Exact-coordinate equality is not a meaningful accessibility score; real proximity/network travel calculation is required before promotion.

batches.title: Ancient woodland status relationship qualification
batches.coverage: Status codes ASNW/PAWS only have candidate meaning after an exact ancient-woodland geometry hit; category data alone is not a parcel result.

batches.title: Conservation area authoritative-document linkage
batches.coverage: Planning Data specification says conservation-area documents provide authoritative context. Candidate use requires exact conservation-area hit plus linked current document; national coverage remains incomplete.

batches.title: Design code relationship and effective-date qualification
batches.coverage: Design codes must be linked from an exact design-code-area hit and checked against start/end dates and document status; current national dataset is small and not proof of absence.

batches.title: Design code status gate: proposed/draft/adopted/withdrawn/informal
batches.coverage: Status must be resolved through the linked design code. Proposed, draft and informal records must never be promoted as adopted policy.

batches.title: Design code rule linkage and rule-applicability gate
batches.coverage: A rule has candidate meaning only after exact area -> design code -> rule linkage and effective-status checks. Rules from unrelated authorities/codes cannot be transferred to the candidate.

batches.title: NSIP decision taxonomy and legacy-value consistency gate
batches.coverage: Current category list uses consent-granted/consent-rejected/withdrawn/appealed, while existing project records may expose legacy values such as Decided/Recommendation. No silent normalization is allowed.

batches.title: NSIP lifecycle-event taxonomy consistency gate
batches.coverage: Infrastructure event codes include legacy/spelling variants. Candidate interpretation requires the actual project log and date sequence; category code alone is not current project status.

batches.title: NSIP project-type linkage
batches.coverage: Project type (transport/energy/etc.) is classification only. Candidate effect requires exact infrastructure-project spatial hit and current project status/decision evidence.

batches.title: Listed building grade linkage with extent guard
batches.coverage: Grade I/II*/II is authoritative classification, but only after the candidate is linked to the relevant listed asset. Outline remains indicative and does not consistently define curtilage.

batches.title: Historic park and garden grade linkage
batches.coverage: Grade is classification only; exact historic park/garden geometry hit and current register record are required before candidate impact is promoted.

batches.title: Minerals plan legal-instrument status linkage
batches.coverage: Dataset contains current, emerging and historical plans. Candidate use requires exact boundary/authority linkage plus start/end/period/document status; a plan record alone is not a site allocation.

batches.title: Waste plan legal-instrument status linkage
batches.coverage: Dataset contains current, emerging and historical waste plans. Exact boundary/authority linkage and plan dates/documents are required; plan membership is not parcel permission.

batches.title: Supplementary plan 2026 legal-status linkage
batches.coverage: Only five supplementary plans are currently present. Candidate use requires correct LPA/plan relationship, examination/adoption status, dates and document; absence cannot prove no relevant supplementary policy.
